rationale: The book's core identification — 'the way' as covenant conduct, the walk, a manner of life measured by God's standard — is the reading the entry's own printed proof texts demand and the reading that best explains the widest span of 'way' language across Scripture. Jeremiah 6:16 ('ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein... We will not walk therein') and Matthew 7:14 (the narrow way that leadeth unto life) are unintelligible as a reference to the person of Christ as such; they are intelligible only as conduct texts, and the christological common interpretation itself lists 'manner of life / path of righteousness' as a recognized common sense (Responses A, B, C all include it). The book goes further and shows the sense is anchored by the first-occurrence definition in Genesis 18:19 ('keep the way of the LORD, to do justice and judgment'), corroborated by 2 Peter 2:21 (the way of righteousness laid beside the holy commandment) and by Paul's own definition of 'the Way' in Acts 24:14 as 'believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets.' Crucially, the book does not deny John 14:6 or Hebrews 10:19-20; it explains them — Christ is the way as covenant conduct embodied and walked perfectly, and coming to the Father 'by him' remains exclusive because there has only ever been one such way, now personed. The strongest counter (the way = the person of Christ as sole means of access through his death and resurrection) explains John 14:6 and Hebrews 10 naturally but must either ignore or silently switch senses for Jeremiah 6:16, Genesis 18:19, Matthew 7:13-14, Psalm 1, Proverbs, and Acts 24:14, i.e., it needs two disconnected meanings where the book needs one meaning plus embodiment. On the supplied evidence the book's core carries the identification better. However, several secondary elaborations (the prosphatos = 'freshly slain' rendering of Hebrews 10:20, flaming sword = word of God, tree = nation, gospel = law of the kingdom) are independent claims of uneven strength and are not established by this entry; support is therefore CORE_ONLY.
book_core_identification: 'The way' as a scriptural symbol denotes covenant conduct — the walk: the God-defined manner of life ('to do justice and judgment,' Gen 18:19), the Torah-shaped path one treads, which Jesus embodies perfectly, so that 'I am the way' means the one covenant-conduct has become a person, not that a person replaces the conduct-sense of the symbol.
book_secondary_elaborations: Hebrews 10:20 prosphatos rendered 'freshly slain' rather than 'new,' making the way a 'freshly-slain and living' road
The derek (way/conduct) vs. mesillah (highway/covenant road) distinction and the reading of Isaiah 35:8-10 through beast/lion symbols (kingdom/ruler)
The door of John 10:9 decoded through Deuteronomy 11:20 (word on the doorposts) and Exodus 12 (blood on the doorposts) as law-plus-lamb
The flaming sword of Genesis 3:24 identified as the word of God (Eph 6:17) preserving, not barring, the way of the tree of life
The compounding of way/truth/life as three aspects of one Torah via Proverbs 6:23
The claim that 'the gospel' means the law of the kingdom (imported from another chapter)
strongest_counter_interpretation: The consensus christological reading: 'the Way' primarily symbolizes Jesus Christ himself — his person, death, and resurrection — as the exclusive means of access to the Father and to salvation (John 14:6; Heb 10:19-20), with the Acts usage ('followers of the Way') as the derivative name of the movement defined by allegiance to that person; OT 'way' texts about conduct are a distinct, subordinate sense that feeds into but does not constitute the titular meaning.
counter_core_identification: 'The Way' = the person of Jesus Christ as the sole path of access to God, grounded in his atoning death and resurrection rather than in a manner of life.
material_core_denial: The counter denies that 'the way' fundamentally symbolizes covenant conduct; it asserts the referent is the person of Christ as means of access, such that conduct texts are a separate homonymous usage rather than the defining content of the symbol Jesus claims in John 14:6.
counter_case: John 14:6 places 'the way' in a first-person identity claim — 'I am the way... no man cometh unto the Father, but by me' — which most naturally identifies a person, not a code of conduct
Hebrews 10:19-20 ties the 'new and living way' explicitly to 'the blood of Jesus' and 'his flesh,' locating the way in the atonement, not in Torah observance
Acts consistently uses 'the Way' as a proper designation for the movement defined by faith in Jesus (Acts 9:2; 19:9, 23; 24:14, 22)
Isaiah 40:3 as applied to John the Baptist makes 'the way of the Lord' the road prepared for the Lord's own coming, i.e., a christological-messianic road
The overwhelming cross-traditional consensus (Catholic, Orthodox, Protestant) reads the term titularly and soteriologically, treating conduct texts as a layered but subordinate sense
book_explanatory_advantages: It explains the entry's own proof texts directly: Jeremiah 6:16's 'good way... walk therein' and Matthew 7:14's narrow way are conduct texts on any reading, and the counter must change senses to handle them

Genesis 18:19 supplies a first-occurrence scriptural definition of 'the way of the LORD' as doing justice and judgment — an explicit in-text key of exactly the kind the book's method (Isa 5:7; 2 Sam 12:7; Ezek 17:12) has already demonstrated Scripture uses

It unifies OT and NT usage under one sense: Psalm 1, Proverbs, Deuteronomy, Jeremiah 6:16, Matthew 7:13-14, Acts 24:14, 2 Peter 2:21, and John 14:6 all read as one symbol (conduct) rather than as a homonym split between 'manner of life' and 'person'

It explains Acts 24:14 verbatim: Paul defines the Way he is charged with as 'believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets' — covenant fidelity, not a new religion — which the sociological-label and titular readings leave as an awkward aside
It preserves rather than denies the exclusivity of John 14:6: the way is exclusive because there is one covenant-conduct, embodied in one person, so 'by me' still holds without remainder

The derek/mesillah distinction and the wedding-garment detail of Matthew 22:11 (being on the highway is not enough; the conduct must match) explain a textual wrinkle the person-only reading does not address
counter_explanatory_advantages: The 'I am' formula of John 14:6 is more immediately personal on the counter reading; the book must add the embodiment step ('the conduct has become a person')
Hebrews 10:19-20's grounding of the way in Jesus' blood and flesh is native to the counter; the book must route it through the Passover-door symbolism and a contested rendering of prosphatos
The Acts absolute usage ('the Way' as a name) is straightforwardly explained by the counter as a title derived from Jesus' self-claim
decisive_sources: Genesis 18:19 — the first-occurrence definition: 'keep the way of the LORD, to do justice and judgment'
Jeremiah 6:16 — the printed proof text: the good way is something one walks in and can refuse to walk in
Matthew 7:13-14 — two ways, two manners of walking, two ends; the entry's second printed text
2 Peter 2:21 — 'the way of righteousness' set in apposition to 'the holy commandment'
Acts 24:14 — Paul defines the Way as believing all things written in the law and the prophets
Proverbs 6:23 — commandment/lamp, law/light, reproofs 'the way of life,' stringing the three titles on one thread
Isaiah 35:8-10 with Matthew 22:9-11 — highway vs. way, and the wedding garment showing road-membership without matching conduct fails
unresolved_objections: The prosphatos = 'freshly slain' rendering of Hebrews 10:20 is lexically contestable: in Koine and LXX usage (e.g., Deut 32:17) the word had generalized to 'new/recent,' so the 'freshly slaughtered way' is an etymologizing elaboration, not an established datum
The identification of the flaming sword of Genesis 3:24 with the word of God via Ephesians 6:17 is suggestive typology, not demonstrated by two independent OT witnesses within this entry
The compounded symbol claims (tree = nation, life = covenant-existence, gospel = law of the kingdom) depend on other chapters not adjudicated here

The book's account of why 'the Way' functions as an absolute proper name in Acts (rather than merely a description of conduct) is thinner than the titular reading's account, even though Acts 24:14 favors the book's content for the name
